pages.headline: India-Canada launch CEPA talks; uranium deal signed
pages.what: During Prime Minister Mark Carney's visit, India and Canada signed Terms of Reference to start CEPA negotiations, aiming at USD 50 billion of trade by 2030. India's Department of Atomic Energy signed a long-term uranium supply contract with Cameco.
key: Terms of Reference for CEPA signed on 2 March 2026
Target: USD 50 billion bilateral trade by 2030
Long-term Cameco uranium contract signed by the DAE
Critical-minerals MoU aligned with G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan
pages.static: A CEPA covers goods, services and investment, going beyond a basic FTA; India's nuclear fuel sourcing depends on safeguarded supply contracts.
pages.angle: Trap: shifting the trade target by a zero.

pages.headline: Finland's President on state visit; strategic partnership
pages.what: President Alexander Stubb's state visit elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability. MoUs covered migration and mobility, environment and statistics, with a Joint Task Force on 6G and a Startup Corridor.
key: Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability
Joint Task Force on 6G; Indo-Finland Startup Corridor
MoUs on migration and mobility, environment, statistics
Stubb was chief guest at the 11th Raisina Dialogue
pages.static: Finland joined the EU in 1995 and NATO in 2023; it is not in EFTA.
pages.angle: Trap: placing Finland in EFTA.

pages.headline: 11th Raisina Dialogue held in New Delhi
pages.what: The 11th Raisina Dialogue, inaugurated by the Prime Minister, ran under the theme 'Samskara - Assertion, Accommodation, Advancement'. It launched a Raisina Science Diplomacy Initiative. Finnish President Alexander Stubb was chief guest.
key: Organisers: MEA and Observer Research Foundation
pages.static: Think-tank-led dialogues such as Shangri-La (IISS) and Raisina (ORF) are Track 1.5 platforms.
pages.angle: Trap: naming another Indian think-tank as co-host.

pages.headline: Modi visits Malaysia; ties deepen
pages.what: Prime Minister Modi visited Malaysia on 7 and 8 February 2026, building on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership of August 2024. Outcomes stressed rules-based maritime order, defence exchanges, digital economy, trade facilitation and semiconductor cooperation.
key: Malaysia sits near the Strait of Malacca
Focus: maritime order, digital economy, semiconductors
Part of India's Act East Policy
pages.static: The Look East Policy of 1992 was recast as the Act East Policy in 2014.
pages.angle: Trap: dating Act East to 1992.

pages.headline: US opens Section 301 probes covering India
pages.what: The USTR started two Section 301 investigations, one on excess industrial capacity (16 partners) and one on forced-labour goods (60 economies). India is named in both and said it stays engaged with Washington.
key: India continues talks on a framework trade agreement
pages.static: Section 301 lets the US impose tariffs on countries found to have unfair trade practices.
pages.angle: Trap: attributing a walkout to India.

pages.headline: US submarine sinks IRIS Dena off Sri Lanka
pages.what: A US Navy submarine sank Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean off Galle. The ship had been at the International Fleet Review 2026 in Visakhapatnam, and Sri Lanka's navy carried out rescue operations.
key: Returning from International Fleet Review 2026, Visakhapatnam
Legal angles: UNCLOS and 1979 SAR Convention (India ratified 2001)
pages.static: UNCLOS 1982 governs rights in maritime zones; the SAR Convention obliges states to assist ships in distress.
pages.angle: Trap: placing the sinking in Indian or Gulf waters.

pages.headline: Force majeure declared as Hormuz shipping stalls
pages.what: Gulf producers declared force majeure after the US-Israel war with Iran disrupted shipping through Hormuz. Around 2.5 to 2.7 million barrels a day of India's oil passes through the strait, and India imports 85-88 per cent of its crude.
key: About 2.5 to 2.7 million barrels a day of India's oil transits Hormuz
Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman
India imports 85-88 per cent of its crude
Several Gulf producers declared force majeure
Force majeure: contractual relief for suppliers
pages.static: The Habshan-Fujairah pipeline lets some UAE crude reach the Gulf of Oman without passing through Hormuz.
pages.angle: Trap: understating India's import dependence.

pages.headline: IEA record stock release; India hesitates
pages.what: The IEA agreed a record 400 million barrel release. India first declined to join, then said it stands ready to act. India holds about 5.33 million tonnes of underground reserves, around 80 per cent full.
key: IEA release: 400 million barrels, a record
Capacity about 5.33 million tonnes, about 80 per cent full
India last joined a coordinated release in 2021
pages.static: The IEA, headquartered in Paris, was set up after the 1973 oil crisis; its members must hold 90 days of net imports.
pages.angle: Trap: calling India a full member.
pages.remember: India: associate, not full, IEA member.

pages.headline: Israel proposes 'Hexagon of Alliances'
pages.what: Israel proposed a 'Hexagon of Alliances' of moderate powers across the Indo-Pacific, Eastern Mediterranean, Gulf and Africa, with Israel, Greece, Cyprus and India as core pillars. It aims to counter Iran's Axis of Resistance, and the Pakistani Senate condemned it.
key: Core pillars: Israel, Greece, Cyprus, India
Spans Indo-Pacific, Eastern Mediterranean, Gulf, Africa
Aims to counter the Iran-led Axis of Resistance
Ethiopia and UAE expected to join
Pakistani Senate passed a resolution condemning it
pages.static: India's I2U2 and IMEC groupings also link India with West Asian partners.
pages.angle: Trap: reversing Pakistan's reaction.
pages.remember: Hexagon: Israel, Greece, Cyprus, India; Pakistan objects.

pages.headline: Kharg Island and Fujairah hit
pages.what: Strikes hit Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90 per cent of Iran's crude exports, and Iran struck oil facilities at Fujairah, the UAE terminal reached by the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline.
key: Kharg Island: about 90 per cent of Iran's crude exports
Iran hit oil facilities at Fujairah, UAE
Fujairah is the second-largest bunkering hub after Singapore
Fujairah lies on the Gulf of Oman
pages.static: Pipelines like East-West (Saudi) and Habshan-Fujairah are the main bypass for Hormuz.
pages.angle: Trap: locating Fujairah inside the Persian Gulf.

pages.headline: Israel destroys Litani bridge in Lebanon
pages.what: Israeli airstrikes destroyed the Qasmiyeh Bridge over the Litani as Israel sought a security zone up to the river. Resolution 1701 sets the area south of the Litani as free of other armed groups.
key: UNSCR 1701 (2006): area free of other armed personnel
Tyre: UNESCO site (1984) near the river mouth
pages.static: UNIFIL was created in 1978 to confirm Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon.
pages.angle: Trap: the Blue Line's parties.

pages.headline: Iran weighs NPT exit; IAEA meets
pages.what: Iran's parliament reviewed NPT withdrawal after strikes on its nuclear sites. The IAEA held an emergency Board meeting at the request of Russia and Iran and reported no damage to sites like Bushehr.
key: IAEA saw no damage at Bushehr; normal radiation
India, Pakistan, Israel, South Sudan never signed the NPT
pages.static: The NPT (1968) recognises five nuclear-weapon states; India rejects it as discriminatory.
pages.angle: Trap: assuming India is an NPT party.
pages.remember: Never signed: India, Pakistan, Israel, South Sudan.

pages.headline: RSP sweeps Nepal elections; Balendra Shah PM
pages.what: The Rastriya Swatantra Party won 182 of 275 seats. Balendra Shah, 35, was sworn in on 27 March as Nepal's youngest and 47th prime minister.
key: Shah sworn in 27 March by President Ram Chandra Paudel
pages.static: Nepal's House of Representatives has 275 members; Nepal became a federal republic in 2008.
pages.angle: Trap: swapping the second and third parties.

pages.headline: Pakistan strikes Afghan Taliban over Durand Line
pages.what: Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab Lil Haq against Afghan Taliban positions as border clashes over fencing and the TTP escalated along the Durand Line.
key: Agreed 1893: Mortimer Durand and Abdur Rahman Khan
pages.static: The McMahon Line (1914) is the India-Tibet boundary; do not confuse it with the Durand Line.
pages.angle: Trap: McMahon or Radcliffe lines.

pages.headline: India holds the BRICS presidency
pages.what: India's 2026 BRICS presidency runs under the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. BRICS+ includes Egypt, the UAE, Ethiopia, Indonesia and Iran.
key: Theme: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
BRICS+: Egypt, UAE, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran
About 49.5 per cent of world population
About 40 per cent of global GDP
pages.static: BRICS began as BRIC in 2006 and added South Africa in 2010.
pages.angle: Trap: calling this India's first chairmanship.

pages.headline: WTO MC14 ends without consensus
pages.what: The conference in Yaounde ended in the early hours of 30 March without consensus. The e-commerce duty moratorium lapsed after 26 years. India opposed incorporating the IFD Agreement.
key: India opposed IFD with about 37 other members
India wants permanent solution on public stockholding
pages.static: Plurilateral agreements within the WTO need consensus to join the framework; India opposes this route.
pages.angle: Trap: saying India backed the IFD.
pages.remember: MC14: moratorium gone; India opposes IFD.

pages.headline: Border trade via Lipulekh set to resume
pages.what: India and China agreed in August 2025 to reopen border trade through Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La. Trade is set to resume in June 2026 after six years. Nepal objects over Lipulekh.
key: Three passes: Lipulekh, Shipki La, Nathu La
Nepal claim rests on Treaty of Sugauli (1816)
pages.static: Border trade marts operate under bilateral agreements; Shipki La was earlier called Pema La.
pages.angle: Trap: swapping passes and States.

pages.headline: Sri Lanka revives Trincomalee oil tank farm project
pages.what: Facing an energy crisis, Sri Lanka is looking to develop the India-backed Trincomalee project. India and Sri Lanka signed a 2022 agreement for joint development of the Trincomalee Oil Tank Farm, built by the British in the 1930s, to raise storage and energy security.
key: Trincomalee: natural harbour on Sri Lanka's north-east coast
2022 India-Sri Lanka agreement on joint development
Oil tank farm built by the British in the 1930s
Goal: more petroleum storage, energy security
pages.static: MAHASAGAR is India's vision for security and growth across the Indian Ocean region.
pages.angle: Trap: crediting Japan for the tank farm.
pages.remember: Trincomalee: British farm, India-Sri Lanka 2022 deal.

pages.headline: Army fields Shaurya drone squadrons
pages.what: The Indian Army began fielding Shaurya Squadrons, dedicated drone sub-units embedded in armoured regiments. Each has 20 to 30 personnel operating surveillance, attack, swarm and FPV drones and loitering munitions, and the plan covers all 67 armoured regiments.
key: Surveillance, attack, swarm, FPV drones, loitering munitions
Five Army commands have inducted them
pages.static: FPV stands for first-person view, where the operator steers the drone through a live camera feed.
pages.angle: Trap: placing them under Army Aviation.

pages.headline: DAC clears Rs 2.38 lakh crore including five more S-400
pages.what: The DAC chaired by Rajnath Singh cleared about Rs 2.38 lakh crore of proposals. These include a fresh batch of five S-400 systems, transport aircraft, remotely piloted strike aircraft and Dhanush guns.
key: AoN for about Rs 2.38 lakh crore
Contract of USD 5.43 billion signed in 2018
pages.static: The DAC is the apex body for capital acquisition; AoN is the first step in the Defence Acquisition Procedure.
pages.angle: Trap: wrong signing year.

pages.headline: INS Dunagiri joins Navy
pages.what: INS Dunagiri is the fifth Project 17A stealth frigate and the second built by GRSE Kolkata, designed by the Warship Design Bureau with about 75 per cent indigenous content.
key: P17A: seven frigates, four Mazagon Dock, three GRSE
pages.static: Warship Design Bureau is the Navy's in-house design organisation.
pages.angle: Trap: yard or class confusion.

pages.headline: Exercises in news: LAMITIYE, Sea Dragon, IMEX
pages.what: LAMITIYE-2026 was India-Seychelles, Sea Dragon a US-led ASW exercise at Guam and IMEX an IONS table-top at Kochi.
key: Contingent: Assam Regiment, INS Trikand, IAF C-130
Sea Dragon: ASW, Andersen AFB, Guam
IOS SAGAR second edition with 16 IONS nations
pages.static: Exercise names are favourite match-the-following material.
pages.angle: Trap: mixing partners.

pages.headline: SIPRI: India second-largest arms importer
pages.what: SIPRI's 2021-25 data show India as the second-largest arms importer with 8.2 per cent, behind Ukraine. Russia supplies about 40 per cent.
pages.static: India's defence import dependence drives Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence.
pages.angle: Trap: naming Saudi Arabia as the top importer.

pages.headline: GTI 2026 puts Pakistan first
pages.what: The Institute for Economics and Peace ranked Pakistan first for the first time and India 13th among 163 countries. Terror deaths fell 28 per cent.
key: Publisher: Institute for Economics and Peace
Deaths down 28 per cent; incidents down 22 per cent
pages.static: Report publishers are a common Prelims target.
pages.angle: Trap: SIPRI versus IEP.

pages.headline: Defence Forces Vision 2047 unveiled
pages.what: The roadmap, prepared by HQ IDS, proposes Space and Cyber Commands and Data, Drone and Cognitive Warfare forces in three phases to 2047.
key: Prepared by HQ Integrated Defence Staff
Space Command, Cyber Command, Data Force, Drone Force
pages.static: The Chief of Defence Staff heads the Department of Military Affairs and is permanent chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee; HQ IDS supports it.
pages.angle: Trap: wrong phase end-year.
